newsitem.title: USA: QUALCOMM files suit against Motorola.
newsitem.headline: QUALCOMM files suit against Motorola.

text.p: QUALCOMM Inc Thursday said it filed a lawsuit against Motorola Inc seeking a declaratory judgment that QUALCOMM's products do not infringe any patents held by Motorola.

In a statement, QUALCOMM said its complaint claims QUALCOMM and Motorola entered into patent and technology license agreements in 1990 that preclude Motorola from asserting infringement of the patents.
Earlier, Motorola said it intends to file a patent infringement suit against QUALCOMM, alleging its Q phone copies the design of Motorola's handheld StarTAC digital cellular phone.

In its complaint, filed in federal court in San Diego, QUALCOMM denies the "Q" Phone infringes any rights of Motorola and requests a judicial finding that QUALCOMM's products are free of any infringement.

"QUALCOMM was careful to respect the intellectual property rights of others, and in the course of designing any new product we seek to ensure that our design does not infringe the rights of any other companies," said Harvey White, president OF QUALCOMM. "In our development of the "Q" Phone we followed our usual practice of verifying and checking existing parents. Our lawsuit seeks judicial confirmation that our judgment was correct."
